[[Intermodal freight transport|Intermodal]] | owner = [[Government of India]] | revenue = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|9023|c}} (2024)[https://www.moneycontrol.com/financials/containercorporationofindia/consolidated-profit-lossVI/CCI#CCI"Financial Results Data from Moneycontrol Site"]. | operating_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|1638|c}} (2024) | net_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|1232|c}} (2024) | assets = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|14038|c}} (2024){{cite web |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/financials/containercorporationofindia/consolidated-balance-sheetVI/CCI#CCI|title=Concor Balance Sheet}} | equity = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|11823|c}} (2024) | num_employees = 1,400 (March 2021) | parent = | subsidiaries = * CONCOR Air Limited * Fresh and Healthy Enterprise Limited * Punjab Logistics Infrastructure Limited * SIDCUL CONCOR Infra Company Limited | website = {{URL|https://concorindia.co.in|concorindia.co.in}} }} '''Container Corporation of India Limited''' ('''CONCOR''') is an Indian [[Public Sector Undertakings in India|public sector undertaking]] which is engaged in transportation and handling of containers. Incorporated in March 1988 under the Companies Act, CONCOR commenced operations in November 1989 taking over an existing network of seven inland container depots (ICDs) from [[Indian Railways]].{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/concor-may-launch-a-container-train-service-between-india-bangladesh/articleshow/62072805.cms|title=CONCOR may launch a container train service between India & Bangladesh|last=Mazumdar|first=Rakhi|date=2017-12-14|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2017-12-29}} == History == CONCOR is one of the Indian public sector undertakings that is currently under consideration for privatisation.{{Cite news |last=PTI |date=12 October 2021 |title=Concor strategic sale not happening this fiscal: DIPAM Secy |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/finance/concor-strategic-sale-not-happening-this-fiscal-dipam-secy/articleshow/86967311.cms |access-date=2022-05-07}} The privatisation process, which involves the [[Government of India|Indian Government]] selling 30.8% out of its shareholding of 54.8%, was initially projected to be completed in the fiscal year 2021–2022, but has since been delayed to the next fiscal year. In April 2022, the Indian Government reduced Indian Railways' land licensing fee from 6% to 3% of the land's market value, which was done to assist the company's privatisation.{{Cite web |last=Asoodani |first=Karishma |date=7 April 2022 |title=Concor disinvestment may progress this month: Sources |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/concor-disinvestment-may-progress-this-month-sources-329079-2022-04-07 |access-date=2022-05-07 |website=Business Today |language=en}} == Operations == CONCOR has multiple operations: [[cargo carrier]]; [[Container terminal|terminal]], warehouse & MMLP operation.{{cite news |title=Concor Registers Significant Turnaround in Business Concor Board Announces Highest Ever Interim Dividend Corporation Records 13.89 Per Cent Increase in its Net Profit in Q3 Investment in Logistic Parks Planned |url=https://pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=69206 |access-date=26 November 2024 |agency=Ministry of Railways, Government of India |publisher=Press Information Bureau |date=20 January 2011}}{{Cite web |date=2024-05-15 |title=Is CONCOR the next big infrastructure bet? |url=https://www.logisticsoutlook.com/logistics/is-concor-the-next-big-infrastructure-bet |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=Logistics Outlook |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=2024-04-13 |title=CONCOR to set up CFS at Kathuwas MMLP in partnership with private firms |url=https://www.maritimegateway.com/concor-to-set-up-cfs-at-kathuwas-mmlp-in-partnership-with-private-firms/ |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=Maritime Gateway |language=en-US}} == Container shipping == As per [[CNN-News18]] report from 19 November 2024, a roadmap study would be commissioned by Container Corporation of India Limited to one of the leading consulting firms, [[Ernst & Young]], [[KPMG]], or [[PwC]], in order to enter the global container shipping industry. The initial target areas will be the Middle East and South Asia.{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Aman |date=19 November 2024 |title=In A First, India Set To Foray Into Global Container Shipping Business {{!}} Exclusive |url=https://www.news18.com/india/in-a-first-india-set-to-foray-into-global-container-shipping-business-exclusive-9124909.html |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=News18 |language=en}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == *[http://www.concorindia.co.in/ Container Corporation of India Ltd.
